<objective>
Stop the D-18 PIN backoff from permanently disabling itself (CR-02) and make
`staff_pin_lock_seconds` agree with `verify_staff_pin` about deactivated profiles (WR-12).

**As a** restaurant owner whose tablet sits on the floor all evening, **I want to** know
that repeated wrong PIN entries keep getting slower forever, **so that** the 10,000-value
PIN space cannot be walked by anyone who picks the tablet up and leaves it running.

Purpose: `least(c_max_lock_seconds, (2 ^ (v_next_attempts - c_free_attempts))::integer)`
applies the `::integer` cast BEFORE `least()` clamps. At the 33rd consecutive wrong attempt
the expression is `2 ^ 31`, which exceeds `int4` and raises `22003`. The raise aborts the
statement, rolling back the very update that would have written `failed_attempts` and
`locked_until` — so the counter freezes at 32, the lock is never re-armed, and from attempt
33 onward the throttle is off while a correct PIN still returns true. Reaching attempt 33
takes roughly 1.7 hours of unattended guessing under the 300-second cap, which is well
inside the threat model D-18 exists for. The existing test drives four failures and never
approaches the boundary.

Output: migration `0005`, an extended backoff suite, and a verified live schema.
</objective>

  <action>
    Create `supabase/migrations/0005_pin_backoff_overflow.sql` as a new additive file. Open it
    with a header comment naming CR-02 and WR-12, stating that it replaces two function bodies
    from `0002` without changing either signature, and stating that `0002` itself is
    deliberately left untouched because it is already applied.

    **`create or replace function public.verify_staff_pin(p_venue_id uuid, p_staff_id uuid, p_pin text)`
    — reproduce the whole body from `0002` with one arithmetic change.**

    CRITICAL: `create or replace function` replaces the ENTIRE definition, and any attribute
    not restated reverts to its default. The replacement must therefore explicitly restate
    `returns boolean`, `language plpgsql`, `security definer` and `set search_path = ''`. A
    SECURITY DEFINER function that loses its empty `search_path` is a privilege-escalation
    hole, and it fails silently — nothing in the suite would notice.

    The arithmetic change: move the `::integer` cast OUTSIDE `least()` so the clamp runs on
    numeric before the narrowing, and additionally clamp the exponent so the power can never
    grow unbounded regardless of the cap's value. The new assignment computes
    `least(c_max_lock_seconds, 2 ^ least(16, v_next_attempts - c_free_attempts))` and casts
    the whole `least(...)` expression to integer. Sixteen keeps the power at 65536 — far
    inside `int4` and far above the 300-second cap — so the clamp can never be reached by the
    exponent path. Leave the `else v_lock_seconds := 0;` branch as it is. Add a comment
    stating why the cast placement is the defect and not a style choice: the raise it caused
    aborted the statement, rolling back the update that writes `failed_attempts` and
    `locked_until`, which is what turned a one-off arithmetic error into a permanently
    disabled rate limiter.

    Preserve every other line of the original body verbatim — the `auth.uid()` null check, the
    `private.get_venue_role` membership gate and its comment about not being a probe oracle,
    the `deactivated_at is null` filter, the `for update` row lock and its comment about two
    rapid taps, the pre-comparison `locked_until` check, the `extensions.crypt` comparison,
    and the success branch that wipes the slate.

    **`create or replace function public.staff_pin_lock_seconds(p_venue_id uuid, p_staff_id uuid)`
    — add the missing filter.** Restate `returns integer`, `language plpgsql`,
    `security definer`, `set search_path = ''` and `stable`. Add
    `and sp.deactivated_at is null` to the `select ... into v_locked_until` predicate so it
    scopes exactly as `verify_staff_pin` does. Without it, a member can read live lock state
    for a profile the owner deactivated — a profile `list_staff_for_pin` deliberately hides —
    which leaks the existence of a deactivated id to anyone who can guess one.

    Re-issue the grant block for both functions after the definitions: revoke EXECUTE from
    `public` first, then from `anon`, then grant to `authenticated` and to `service_role`.
    Revoking from `public` before `anon` is the operative ordering — reversed, `anon` inherits
    from `public` and the second revoke is a no-op. `create or replace` does preserve the
    existing ACL, so this is defensive rather than required; keep it so the file reads as a
    complete statement of the functions' exposure.

    Restate both `comment on function` statements, amending the `verify_staff_pin` comment to
    say the backoff is bounded at both ends.

    Extend `tests/staff/pin-verify-backoff.test.ts` with the cases in `&lt;behavior&gt;`. Preset
    `failed_attempts` and clear `locked_until` through `typedAdmin` as fixture setup — that is
    ground-truth mutation, not an authorization assertion, so it stays inside the
    `tests/rls/setup.ts` rule — and drive every actual verification through the device
    member's anon-key client so the RPC is exercised as a real principal. Read the row back
    through `typedAdmin` to assert `failed_attempts` and `locked_until`. Assert
    `error` is null explicitly on every call, because CR-02's most misleading symptom is that
    the RPC starts raising where its own contract says it never does.

    Write the 32-boundary and 40-boundary cases RED FIRST, against the CURRENT schema — with
    `0001` through `0004` applied and `0005` either not yet written or written but NOT yet
    applied. Run them in that state and confirm both fail with SQLSTATE `22003`
    (`integer out of range`). Only then apply `0005` with
    `/opt/homebrew/bin/supabase migration up`, reload the PostgREST cache, and re-run the same
    two cases green.

    Do not apply `0005` before the RED run. `0005` IS the arithmetic change, so applying it
    first means the cases never observe the defect, and a regression test that never
    reproduced the defect proves nothing. Record the observed `22003` failure in the plan
    summary as evidence the RED run actually happened.
  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| tablet -> `verify_staff_pin` | Any signed-in principal reaches this RPC at `/rest/v1/rpc/verify_staff_pin`; the membership gate inside it is the only boundary. |
| tablet -> `staff_pin_lock_seconds` | Same exposure; it returns state about a row the caller cannot otherwise select. |
| migration file -> live database | A replaced SECURITY DEFINER function runs as its owner; an omitted attribute in the replacement is a silent privilege change. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01G-15 | Elevation of Privilege | `verify_staff_pin` backoff arithmetic | critical | mitigate | CR-02: the `int4` overflow at attempt 33 aborts the statement, rolling back the write that re-arms the lock, so the throttle permanently disables itself while a correct PIN still returns true — an unthrottled oracle over a 10,000-value space. Task 1 clamps before casting and caps the exponent at 16. Proven closed by the 32- and 40-boundary tests asserting a null error AND a re-armed `locked_until`, not merely that the call returned. |
| T-01G-16 | Denial of Service | `verify_staff_pin` contract | medium | mitigate | The raise also broke the documented invariant that the function never raises, so a wrong PIN surfaced to the waiter as a generic error rather than the wrong-PIN copy. Same fix; the tests assert `error` is null on every call. |
| T-01G-17 | Information Disclosure | `staff_pin_lock_seconds` | low | mitigate | WR-12: the missing `deactivated_at` filter leaks the existence of a deactivated profile id to any venue member. Task 1 adds the filter so the two functions treat deactivated profiles identically. |
| T-01G-18 | Elevation of Privilege | `create or replace function` attribute loss | high | mitigate | Replacing a function restates its whole definition; omitting `set search_path = ''` on a SECURITY DEFINER function is a search-path-injection hole that no existing test would notice. Task 1 restates every attribute and Task 2 verifies `prosecdef` and `proconfig` directly against `pg_proc` rather than trusting the file. |
| T-01G-19 | Tampering | migration application | high | mitigate | A phase can pass build and typecheck against a database that never received the migration, because types come from the committed file. Task 2 is BLOCKING, applies the migration, reloads the PostgREST cache, and re-reads the live catalog. |
</threat_model>
